title: RescueSpeech: A German Corpus for Speech Recognition in Search and Rescue Domain
manual_evidence: Zenodo describes authentic German speech from simulated search-and-rescue exercises and explicitly states that the dataset contains manually annotated recordings from native German speakers. The v2 deposit exposes Readme.md plus Task_ASR.tar.gz and Task_enhancement.tar.gz; ASR contains 2,412 clean utterances and synthetic noisy counterparts. Exact file-level scope and annotation unit of the human annotation have not yet been isolated.
inclusion_rationale: Primary non-singing German production with an explicitly stated manually annotated subset and a public authoritative repository deposit.
decision_note: Do not admit to core until the manual subset and annotation method are isolated at file level. Synthetic noisy augmentations are derivative and must not be treated as additional primary productions; any automatic-only material remains outside core.
next_action: Enumerate archive contents without committing large audio; parse README/manifests/transcription metadata; identify which 2,412 clean utterances carry manual annotation, annotation granularity (transcript vs temporal/phonetic), speaker IDs and license/redistribution terms; then ingest only eligible original/manual observations with authoritative checksums.
dedup_note: No known recording-lineage duplicate identified in current registry; synthetic noisy copies must link back to the same underlying clean utterances rather than count as independent productions.
